D.t: Seth Bodnar trails by 18.3 and wins 0% of simulations. Closing it takes about 51,783 voters switching sides, or 103,566 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +24.6 and R +11.9. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is D +4.4. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Bodnar (D) at D +12.3; your worst is American Pulse Research & Polling for NonStop Local at D +0.7. 8 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Missoula, a projected net 18,200 votes; Gallatin, a projected net 4,676 votes; Silver Bow, a projected net 3,194 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Gallatin, D +7.2, 11.5% of the vote; Lewis and Clark, D +1.3, 7.0% of the vote; Park, R +2.5, 1.9% of the vote; Hill, R +10.2, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Seth Bodnar runs furthest behind in Sanders, Madison, Fergus. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 93% of voters, 29 to 20, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.64 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 71% of voters, 29 to 20, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.56 points; Midsize counties, 61% of voters, 33 to 23, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.06 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Seth Bodnar: Immigration voters 13 to 9, Small counties 24 to 17, Voters who can afford daily costs 25 to 17. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$999K cash against $1.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.1 points away from Seth Bodnar. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
